gpt.text:
Run those three commands in order; they’re set up to (1) pick the best module candidate via AUB, (2) run system-level candidates, then (3) generate the next prioritized fix report.

## 1) Module-level autopilot (AUB) + select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
**What it does**
- Executes AUB experiments defined in the module registry.
- Compares candidates against the current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`).
- `--select-best` typically updates the champion pointer/artifact to the best-performing candidate (depending on your tool’s behavior: it may overwrite a symlink, write a new `champion_*.json`, and/or update a registry entry).

**After it finishes**
- Check the produced report/output path (usually printed at the end).
- Confirm the “best” selection actually improved the target metric(s) you care about (mean/min and any guardrails).

## 2) System-level autopilot (system candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
**What it does**
- Runs end-to-end/system experiments defined in `system_candidates.yaml`.
- This is usually slower and more holistic than module-level A/B.

**After it finishes**
- Verify whether any system candidate beats the updated champion (if step 1 changed it).
- If your tooling doesn’t auto-promote system candidates, note the best candidate ID/path for manual promotion.

## 3) Generate “next fix” report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
**What it does**
- Analyzes recent experiment outcomes and registry status.
- Produces a concrete to-do list in `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` (usually pointing to weakest areas, failing tests, or low-min regressions).

## Recommended quick checks (before/after)
- Ensure your working tree is clean (or at least you’ve committed the current champion baseline).
- Capture logs/artifacts from both autopilots (CI artifacts or local run folder).
- If `--select-best` promotes a new champion, commit the changed champion file(s) and any updated registry pointers so the handoff is reproducible.

If you paste the stdout summary (or the generated report paths) from step 1 and step 2, I can tell you whether the promotion looks sane (e.g., mean improved but min regressed) and what to do next.
